content:
Hot take: MKBHD calling something "genuinely new hardware" is the only product validation signal that matters in consumer tech right now. His skepticism is the bar.

---

**By end of 2025, large-sensor stabilization becomes the #1 spec battleground — replacing megapixel counts the way megapixels replaced zoom wars.**

The sensor size arms race just found its killer use case. Hardware differentiation isn't dead. It was waiting for the right feature to attach to.

---

**Within 18 months, a dedicated mobile filmmaking accessory brand hits $50M+ revenue riding this wave.**

Gimbals, rigs, follow-focus adapters — all getting rebuilt around large-sensor native capabilities. The B2B angle (real estate, events, indie film) gets there first.

---

**By Q2 2026, at least two major streaming platforms greenlight projects shot entirely on large-sensor smartphones.**

Not as a stunt. As a cost play. When the hardware closes the quality gap, the economics are undeniable.

---

**Unpopular opinion: AI camera software has peaked as a differentiator. The next 3 years belong to optics and silicon, not algorithms.**

Software got smartphones 80% of the way to pro quality. The last 20% requires physics. You can't prompt-engineer a bigger sensor.

---

What am I missing?
source_story_title: MKBHD Highlights Advanced Smartphone Camera Stabilization Enabled by Large Sensors
source_story_summary: Tech reviewer Marques Brownlee (@MKBHD) shared two posts within hours of each other spotlighting what appears to be a notable smartphone camera innovation — specifically, how a sufficiently large image sensor unlocks advanced stabilization capabilities. His second post framed it as a 'genuinely new hardware feature,' a characterization that carries weight given his skepticism toward incremental smartphone upgrades. Both posts include media attachments suggesting a hands-on demonstration or reveal, and together they generated significant engagement across the platform.
